issues.description: reload() lacks a stated invariant about atomicity of the clear-then-reload sequence
issues.detail: The reload method clears marks before parsing the new file. If _init_lineparser or _parse_line raises (corrupt file, IO error mid-read), the manager is left with an empty marks dict and a single 'changed' emit will not have fired. State the invariant: either marks are fully replaced atomically, or the prior state is preserved on failure. Currently neither holds.

issues.description: Command naming is inconsistent with sibling commands (snake vs hyphen, singular vs plural)
issues.detail: Existing commands are quickmark_save, quickmark_load, bookmark_add, bookmark_load (singular). The new commands are quickmarks_reload and bookmarks_reload (plural). The feature files also write :bookmarks-reload and :quickmarks-reload. A reader auditing the command surface will trip on this. Pick one convention and document it; the cost of fixing now is one rename.

issues.description: reload() emits changed even when contents are unchanged; no diffing invariant stated
issues.detail: Every reload unconditionally emits self.changed, regardless of whether marks actually differ from the prior state. For a literate reader, the postcondition should be stated: 'changed is emitted iff marks differ'. If observers are cheap, leave it; if not, document why the unconditional emit is correct. Either way, name the contract.

issues.description: Test does not verify the failure-mode invariant
issues.detail: test_reload only covers the happy path: write, reload, observe new contents. There is no test for what happens when the on-disk file is malformed or unreadable during reload. Given that reload is now user-invokable at arbitrary times, the failure behavior is part of the contract and should have at least one test asserting either rollback or documented-empty semantics.

issues.description: Extracted reload() duplicates the parse loop verbatim without a literate comment
issues.detail: The parse loop ('skip blank/comment lines, then _parse_line') is now the body of reload() and was previously the body of __init__. The extraction is correct, but a one-line docstring sentence stating the file format contract ('one mark per non-blank non-comment line; comments start with #') would let the next reader follow without grepping _parse_line. Cheap to add.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED. The refactor extracting reload() is sound and the diff is small, but the new public reload contract is not stated: clear-then-parse is not atomic on failure, the 'changed' signal fires unconditionally, and the failure mode is untested. Naming also drifts from sibling commands (quickmarks_reload vs quickmark_save), which a literate reader will notice immediately. None of these block correctness on the happy path; all are cheap to fix and would move this from "tried correct" to "proved correct" for the file-IO edge cases that reload uniquely exposes.
